claims.text: Give empirically in all cases w/o waiting for culture: it neutralizes only circulating toxin not yet bound to or within cells.
claims.quote: Diphtheria antitoxin must be administered empirically in all cases of diphtheria without waiting for culture confirmation because the antitoxin neutralizes only circulating toxin not yet bound to or within cells (2).

claims.text: Early administration mitigates the toxin's effects and improves outcomes.
claims.quote: Early administration of antitoxin mitigates the effects of the toxin and improves outcomes

claims.text: US: obtained from the CDC through an expanded access IND (EA-IND).
claims.quote: In the United States, antitoxin must be obtained through an expanded access investigational new drug (EA-IND) from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) (4).

claims.text: Equine origin: a skin (or conjunctival) test to rule out sensitivity should always precede administration.
claims.quote: CAUTION: Diphtheria antitoxin is of equine origin (ie, derived from horses); therefore, a skin (or conjunctival) test to rule out sensitivity should always precede administration.

claims.text: Allergic reactions: anaphylaxis within 30 minutes and delayed serum sickness (type III hypersensitivity).
claims.quote: Allergic reactions include anaphylaxis occurring within 30 minutes of administration and delayed allergic reactions (serum sickness, a type III hypersensitivity reaction).

claims.text: Abx are required to eradicate the organism and prevent spread; they aren't substitutes for antitoxin.
claims.quote: Antibiotics are required to eradicate the organism and prevent spread; they are not substitutes for antitoxin.
